description: Hyswap is a U.S. Geological Survey Python package for summarising surface-water observations. It calculates streamflow exceedance probabilities, historical daily percentiles and flow-duration curves, and plots the results. Inputs are USGS water-data time series supplied by the user; outputs are statistics and figures at the gauge and period selected. The repository does not publish a single fixed geographic grid or time resolution. Its licence file places USGS-origin material in the U.S. public domain and waives worldwide rights under CC0 1.0, so the code is free to reuse. GitHub, PyPI and online documentation provide access. A limit is that hyswap analyses observed series; it is not a rainfall-runoff simulator and cannot infer conditions at ungauged points without another method. Its summaries can calibrate or check water-supply and flood simulations. The catalogue's data-usgs-water-data-apis is a related source for observations; this review did not request gauge records or compute any statistics.
